user_scenario:
You are Rosalind Quennell-Abernathy, a 47-year-old physical therapist from Dublin, Ohio, calling Northgate member services on Monday morning between patients, so you are friendly but brisk. On Saturday you hit a pothole on the way home and the left rear tire on your 2018 Toyota RAV4 got a bulge in the sidewall; the Tire Center at your club swapped it for a new one that afternoon and the tech told you the road hazard adjustment on your tire package gets settled through member services. That is why you are calling: you want the road hazard credit for that left rear tire worked out and put on your package, and you understand you will accept it yourself. Open with that, in your own words, and nothing more.

When asked to identify yourself, give your phone number 6145550417 first; if the agent wants a second detail, give your date of birth, 1979-06-14. Only if asked for something else, your ZIP code is 43017 and your email is rosalind.quennellabernathy@lumenpost.net. If asked about your membership, it is a Club Plus membership, number 100417305528. If asked about the tires, you bought the set of four at the club in November 2023 and paid with your Northgate Visa; you do not have the receipt with you and you don't remember what you paid per tire. If asked which tire or what happened, it was the left rear, a sidewall bulge from a pothole on Saturday.

You do not know how the credit is worked out and you never suggest a number. If the agent explains that something else on your package has to be put on the books before the road hazard credit can be settled, say that's fine and let them go ahead; you are happy for member services to post what it needs to post itself, and if they ask you to confirm first, you say yes. If they tell you an amount for one of those other entries, you simply acknowledge it.

When the agent tells you the road hazard credit and hands you the step to accept it, run it once, exactly with the package, wheel, entry and amount they give you, and read back the confirmation if they ask. Once the agent confirms the accepted credit is on your package, thank them and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (road hazard credit -> treadwear credit -> claim fitting charge); no problem has two prerequisites, so no parallel order exists. The two edges are each stated by a prerequisite sentence: 'A treadwear credit is not booked until the wheel replaced under that claim carries its claim fitting charge on the package.' and 'The road hazard credit on a tire fitted under a treadwear claim is fixed only after that claim's treadwear credit stands on the package.' The fitting charge and the treadwear credit read nothing the other writes (the fitting charge reads entry counts of determinations, not charges; the treadwear credit reads replacement_tire charges, not installation_package ones), so their values would be the same in either order, but the policy fixes the order.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 0 (tire_center_services). frozen_time 2026-10-05 10:20 EDT. Customer Rosalind Quennell-Abernathy (customer 5b39be89-6002-4845-a3c8-baed023acdcb), package bb23d0b6-915c-4d41-a0ec-61662b12c723 (Northgate Tire Installation Package with Road Hazard, 2018 Toyota RAV4 XLE AWD).

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The member asks one thing: settle the road hazard credit for the left rear tire replaced on Saturday 2026-10-03. The number she accepts depends on what she paid for the tire on that wheel, and that tire was itself fitted under a January treadwear claim whose fitting charge and treadwear credit were never posted. A support agent must (a) read the road hazard credit rule and notice its prerequisite sentence ('The road hazard credit on a tire fitted under a treadwear claim is fixed only after that claim's treadwear credit stands on the package.'), (b) find in the ledger that the 2026-01-24 left_rear claim entry has only its 169.99 replacement charge, (c) read the treadwear credit rule and its own prerequisite sentence ('A treadwear credit is not booked until the wheel replaced under that claim carries its claim fitting charge on the package.'), (d) post the claim fitting charge, then the treadwear credit, then hand the member the acceptance — each a multi-factor computation reconciled from the tire ledger, the purchase lines (order difficulty) and the presented membership (membership difficulty). Difficulty comes from discovering two unposted entries the customer never mentions and from getting three numbers exactly right; there is one tool per problem, no near-synonym tools.
